passages.heard: This little girl has 53 cents worth of stamps stuck to her coat, and she's about to be mailed.  Like a package her parents are sending her to her grandparents 73 miles away.

It's 1914 in Idaho, a year earlier, America launched parcel post and people noticed something.  The rules never actually said you couldn't mail a person.  The very first baby was carried by a mailman to his grandma's house for 15 cents.

It sounds like a joke.  It wasn't.  May rode in the mail car of a train, right next to the letters and parcels, through the  hills of Idaho, and guess who was looking after her?  The mail clerk on board was her relative.
You see, to the post office, she was just a very heavy parcel, under the weight limit,  stamped, and addressed, so, legally, she was mail.
When the postmaster general heard about it, he banned mailing people, but the next year,  another little girl still rode a mail train, 720 miles, her postage, just 15 cents.
